messages:
maria: Heads-up — ticket #4872 from Sam-CS: AcmeHealth saw a big wave of 429s this morning around 07:12 PST during their scheduled ETL burst. They claim quota was exhausted even though their recent usage was normal.
sam-cs: Customer's logs attached in the ticket: intermittent 429s for ~6m, then traffic resumed. They also said billing looked normal. Asking for a quick triage. :eyes:
kevin: I'm seeing a correlated spike in limiter drops for tenant `acme_health` at 07:12:11 UTC in the global limiter metrics. 429s map to token_bucket.rejected.
sanjay: Can you paste the limiter snapshot? want to see refill rate and burst tokens at the time.
kevin: Pasting relevant snippet from the limiter debug stream:
```
[07:12:10] tenant=acme_health tokens=0 capacity=100 refill_per_second=0.0 last_refill=1610009878
[07:12:10] incoming=350 request_rate=5.8sps dropped=342
[07:12:11] audit: migration_flag=billing-migration-v2 applied -> quota_multiplier=0.0
```
Kept the full log in the ticket.
maria: Refill_per_second=0.0 ? that looks wrong. Was there a billing migration this morning?
sanjay: Yes — there was a config migration rolling out that maps old billing credits into the new tenant credit system. Looks like a transform accidentally set quota_multiplier to 0 for tenants without explicit migrated credits. That would instantly prevent refill.
kevin: That explains the 429s. The traffic pattern was a legit burst from their ETL job, which normally gets filled from bucket but here refill stopped so bucket hit 0 and we started rejecting.
sam-cs: Acme says this caused client errors and some downstream retries that amplified the issue. They asked if we can backfill and who to escalate to for billing credit adjustments.
maria: Immediate mitigation options?
kevin: Short term: emergency override to treat `billing-migration-v2` flag as passthrough — i.e., don't set multiplier to 0. I can push a hotfix to limiter-config to default multiplier to 1 for tenants without migrated credits.
sanjay: Also can we add a safety that prevents multiplier <= 0 from being applied in runtime? A hard guard.
kevin: Agreed. I'll open a quick PR and deploy to canary.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline queued for keys: limiter-config-pr-1456. Tests: unit+integrations.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy to cluster us-west-2a started.
kevin: Canary looks healthy after 90s, reverted multipliers back to 1 for acme_health. Monitoring showing token refill resumed and 429s stopped.
sam-cs: I've told Acme we've applied a temporary override and we're working on root cause. They asked for a timeline for permanent fix and billing backfill.
maria: For billing/backfill — finance/CS to coordinate. From infra side, we should propose: 1) immediate credit backfill for affected window 2) waive overage fees for the incident period.
sanjay: Permanent fix: (A) validate the migration transform so tenants without migrated credits keep prior quota (B) add runtime guard to reject unsafe multipliers (C) add unit+integration test for migration case. Also add canary gate for future migrations.
kevin: New alerts to add: threshold on `tenant_quota_exhaustion_rate` per-tenant: fire if > 0.2 for 30s; alert to #eng-sre and #support with tenant tag. Also an automated runbook link in alert with one-click override to restore multiplier.
maria: I'll draft the support playbook steps and rollback checklist: investigate ticket, check limiter snapshot, if multiplier<=0 do emergency override, notify customer, escalate to eng.
kevin: Repro steps for engineering (so we can test and close):
1) Simulate tenant with capacity=100, refill_per_second=1.
2) Apply migration transform that sets multiplier=0 for tenant.
3) Drive a burst: `wrk -t2 -c50 -d10s http://api/redwood/v1/generate` and observe token_bucket.rejected > 0 and 429s.
4) Apply hotfix to default multiplier to 1 and confirm refill resumes.

sanjay: I'll own the PR and add the migration unit tests. Kevin will handle the alert+runbook and the emergency override tooling. Maria will own customer comms and playbook. Sam-CS will coordinate billing/backfill.
maria: One more follow-up: let's add a retrospective bullet to consider conservative defaults during big migrations (no zeroing). Also add a postmortem link in the ticket.
kevin: I'll create the incident postmortem draft after the PR merges, include graphs (token counts, 429 rate, customer retry loop) and proposed mitigations.
sam-cs: Acme appreciated the quick patch. They've requested a written timeline for backfill by EOD. Filing that with finance now.
maria: Thanks all — closing this thread here. Will paste the postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
